desc:
Adding features to your React Native app is how a live product keeps improving without a rewrite. Ecom Swift LLC reads your existing code, builds new screens, flows or fixes inside your project, tests them on iOS and Android and opens a pull request for you.

## What does it mean to add features to a React Native app?

It means extending an app that already exists, using its current structure, rather than starting over. A feature can be a new screen, a changed flow, a fix to something broken or a connection to an extra backend call. The work arrives as a pull request, so your team can read every change before it joins the main branch.

Working inside an existing project calls for a different habit than building a new one. The developer must follow your naming, state handling and folder layout, so the new code looks like it belongs.

## Why do live apps stall without regular feature work?

Users compare your app with the ones they use every day. When a requested option stays missing for months, they leave reviews, switch to a competitor or stop opening the app. Meanwhile your own list of ideas grows, and nobody has time to build it.

Small, scoped packages break that jam. You pick a handful of changes, agree them in writing and receive working, tested code. That keeps momentum without hiring a full-time developer or opening a long contract.

## How careful feature work protects what already works

A new feature touches old code. A change to a shared component, a navigation rule or an API call can break a screen nobody remembered. That is why the first step is reading the code, and the last step is testing the existing journeys, not only the new one.

Loading and error states matter too. A screen that works on fast Wi-Fi but freezes on a weak connection will frustrate users. Handling empty results, failed calls and slow responses makes the feature feel finished. The effect on retention and reviews depends on what you build, but a stable release is always the base.

## What good feature delivery includes

- A written description of each feature, agreed before coding starts.
- Code that matches your existing patterns, folder structure and naming.
- New screens with loading, empty and error states handled.
- API calls to your backend with sensible failure messages.
- A pull request that explains each change and the reason behind it.
- Testing on both iOS and Android, on small and large screens.
- A short written summary of changes for your records.
- Automated tests for new code in the larger package.
- A release build for both stores when the package includes it.
- A handover call so your team understands the new parts.

## What we do

You send the repository and a list of changes. We read the project, ask questions and write each feature in plain language for your approval. We then build on a separate branch so your main code stays safe.

Basic covers one feature or a few small fixes. Standard covers a full flow with up to three new screens and API calls. Premium covers a larger set with automated tests, a release build and a handover call. If the list is bigger than the package, we tell you before starting and suggest which items to include first.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe each change by what the user should be able to do.
- Share designs or screenshots when you have them.
- Tell us which services and keys the feature needs.
- Review the pull request and test it on your own phone.
- Keep a list of future requests so the next package is easy to scope.

**Avoid:**
- Sending a vague list such as make it better.
- Changing the requirements halfway through a feature.
- Merging untested code straight into the release branch.
- Asking for a redesign inside a small fix package.
- Forgetting that a paid third-party service has its own account and cost.

## Who this service is for

An owner whose app was built by someone else and who needs a reliable developer for the next changes. A small team that has ideas but no spare engineering time. A founder who needs one specific flow, such as a booking screen or a settings page, added to a live product.

## What we need from you

Repository access as a collaborator, a clear list of changes and any designs, API documentation or test accounts. We never need your passwords. Store access is only needed if you want a release uploaded, and it can be granted as a limited developer role.
